posts.caption: Black Gram Vada (Prasad Style)
posts.fullCaption:
Black Gram Vada (Prasad Style)

Traditionally offered as Prasad in Hanuman and Venkateswara Balaji temples, often strung together as Vada Mala garlands for Hanuman . 

The crisp bite, peppery aroma, and ghee‑infused flavor make them a favorite both in temples and homes. 

Ingredients

• 500 g black gram (whole or split black urad dal)
• 50 ml ghee
• 2 tsp (≈12 g) salt
• 2 tsp (≈5 g) cumin seeds
• 3 tsp (≈11 g) black pepper
• Pinch of hing (asafoetida)

Method

1. Place the black gram in hot water for 30–45 minutes only. Do not over‑soak.
2. Drain completely and grind coarsely without adding water , with salt ,cumin, black pepper, and hing.
3. Heat ghee until hot, pour it over the mixture, and mix well.
4.Take small portions, roll into balls, and press flat on a baking sheet or plate to desired thickness. .

* Thin vadas → crispier texture
* Thicker vadas → softer inside

5. Deep fry on medium flame until golden brown.

posts.caption: 🌱 Coriander Rice (Khotimeera Annam)
posts.fullCaption:
🌱 Coriander Rice (Khotimeera Annam)

✨ A fragrant, flavorful rice dish that’s quick to make - Can be enjoyed as it is or pairs beautifully with yogurt or dal.

Ingredients
• 200 g rice (cook & cool )
• 3–4 green chilies (adjust to taste)
• 3–4 garlic cloves
• 2 tbsp white sesame
• 100 g fresh coriander leaves
• 2 tbsp oil
• 2 tsp salt

Tempering:
• 1 tsp urad dal
• 1 tsp chana dal

Method
1. Heat oil, fry chilies & garlic lightly.
2. Add sesame, fry till golden.
3. Add chopped coriander leaves, sauté 2 mins. Cool & coarsely grind.
4. In a pan, heat oil, fry urad & chana dal till golden.
5. Add ground coriander mix + salt, sauté briefly.
6. Mix in rice, toss well.

posts.caption: Crispy Ragi Spinach Balls
posts.fullCaption:
Crispy Ragi Spinach Balls

Love the earthy goodness of ragi? These balls are crispy outside, soft inside, and perfect to enjoy plain as they are or with peanut chutney, pickle, or your favorite sauce. Best eaten hot for crunch, though they turn soft and comforting when cool. You can also add spinach, grated carrot, or grated bottle gourd for extra flavor and nutrition.
Ingredients
• 1 glass ragi flour
• 1 glass sour buttermilk
• 1 glass water
• 3–4 green chilies, finely chopped
• 1 medium onion, finely chopped
• 1 bunch spinach, blanched & chopped
• A handful of coriander leaves, finely chopped
• 2–3 tbsp oil
Method
1. In a pan, mix ragi flour, buttermilk, water, green chilies, onion, spinach, coriander, and oil.
2. Cook on medium flame, stirring continuously, until it forms a firm dough. Keep adding a little oil to avoid sticking.
3. Cover and let it rest until warm.
4. Knead well, then shape into small balls.
5. Cook by one of these methods:• Air fry at 170°C for 10–12 minutes
• Deep fry until golden brown
• Shallow fry in a pan with little oil.

posts.caption: Air-Fried Crispy Poha
posts.fullCaption:
Air-Fried Crispy Poha
A light, crunchy, and flavorful snack made with minimal ingredients—healthy, tasty, and absolutely addictive! Perfect for tea-time, travel, or guilt-free munching anytime.

Ingredients
• 250 g poha (flattened rice)
• 1 cup peanuts (75 g)
• 1 cup cashews (75 g)
• 1 cup roasted chana dal (50 g)
• 8–10 green chillies, slit lengthwise
• A handful of curry leaves
• 2 tbsp oil
• ½ tsp hing (asafoetida)
• ¼ tsp turmeric powder
• Salt to taste
(Optional: add makhana and puffed rice for extra crunch)
Method
1. Air-fry separately at 180°C:
• Poha: 5–8 minutes until crisp
• Peanuts & cashews: 5 minutes until golden
• Roasted chana dal: 2 minutes

2. Prepare seasoning:
• Heat oil in a pan.
• Fry green chillies until slightly crisp.
• Add curry leaves; fry until crunchy.
• Stir in hing and turmeric.

3. Mix & coat:
•Combine roasted poha, peanuts, cashews, and chana dal.
• Add salt and seasoning.
• Toss well until evenly coated.

posts.caption: Crispy Sesame (Til) Chikki – Traditional Sweet Treat
posts.fullCaption:
Crispy Sesame (Til) Chikki – Traditional Sweet Treat
This is one of my all‑time favorites! I’ve always bought sesame (til) chikki from stores, but tried making it at home for the first time — and wow, it tastes so fresh, good, and crispy. Truly one of the easiest sweets to make!
You can also add sunflower seeds, pumpkin seeds, or peanuts for extra crunch and flavor.
Ingredients
• 150 g roasted sesame seeds (til)
(gas top / 180°C – 5 mins)
• 100 g jaggery
• ¼ cup water (≈ 50 ml)
• 1 tsp ghee
1. Add water and jaggery to a pan.
• Boil until jaggery melts.
• If impurities appear, strain and return to the pan.
• Continue boiling until it reaches a soft , firm ball consistency (test by dropping a little syrup in cold water — it should form a firm ball).
2. Mix with Sesame• Add roasted sesame seeds to the hot jaggery syrup.
• Stir quickly so all seeds are evenly coated. Cook for 1-2 mins.
3. Grease a plate with ghee and transfer the mixture.
• Place a greased paper or plate on top and press to desired thickness.
• Alternatively, grease a rolling pin and roll while mixture is still medium hot.
4. Cut or Shape• While still warm, mark lines for cutting.
• Once cooled, break into pieces.
• Optionally, grease your hands and shape into til laddus (balls) while mixture is safe to handle.
Tips
• Always test jaggery syrup consistency; undercooked syrup makes sticky chikki, overcooked makes it too hard.
• Store in an airtight container to keep crisp.

posts.caption: Minty Chana Yogurt Bowl
posts.fullCaption:
Minty Chana Yogurt Bowl
A refreshing, protein-packed snack bursting with flavor and crunch!

Ingredients:
• 1 cup cooked chickpeas (chana)
• 1 tbsp coriander-mint chutney
• 2 tbsp thick yogurt
• ½ cup finely chopped cucumber
• 1 tomato, chopped
• 1 small onion, chopped
• ½ tsp chaat masala
Method:
1. Soak chana overnight and pressure cook for 3–4 whistles with a pinch of salt.
2. In a bowl, take 1 cup of boiled chana.
3. Add coriander mint chutney, yogurt, cucumber, tomato, and onion.
4. Mix everything well until coated.
5. Sprinkle chaat masala on top.
6. Serve chilled or at room temperature. Enjoy the burst of flavors !

After a little break, I’m back with a quick and delicious treat that’s perfect for snacking or everyday cravings! This crunchy makhana recipe tastes just like caramel popcorn—but with a wholesome desi twist. Ready in minutes, and totally addictive!

Caramel Makhana Crunch
Ingredients:
• Makhana (Fox Nuts) – 100 g
• Til (Sesame Seeds) – 50 g
• Jaggery – 150 g
• Ghee – 1 tsp
• Water – ½ cup
Instructions:
1. Dry roast makhana and sesame seeds separately in an air fryer or on gas.
* Makhana should be crispy.
* Sesame seeds should turn light brown and aromatic.
2. In a wide pan, add water and grated jaggery.
* Simmer on low flame until it thickens and forms sticky drops from the ladle.
3. Add ghee, roasted sesame, and makhana. Mix well to coat evenly.
4. Transfer to a plate while still warm (or it may stick to the pan).
5. Let it cool completely and store in an airtight container.
Ready in minutes, this crunchy delight is perfect for guilt-free snacking!

posts.fullCaption:
Palli podi 
Palli Podi a delicious and versatile spice blend! Can be eaten with hot rice and ghee, idli , dosa or as a seasoning for veggies and poha. The aroma and taste are incredible!

Ingredients
- 250gms peanuts
- 1 tablespoon (20gms) chili powder
- 4-5 dry red chilies
- 2 teaspoons (5gms) cumin seeds (Jeera)
- 2 tablespoons (10gms) coriander seeds (Dhania)
- 3 tablespoons (30gms) sesame seeds (TIL)
- 5-6 cloves garlic (20gms) (optional)
- 2 teaspoons (12gms) salt
- 2 tablespoons (15gms) dry coconut (optional)

1. Dry roast the peanuts, in oven (180C 12-15 mins) or gas top on medium flame 
2.Dry sesame seeds and dry red chillies in a pan until fragrant.
3. Dry roast coriander seeds, cumin seeds for 1- 2 mins and desiccated coconut ( few secs)
4. Let them cool completely.
5. Grind the mixture into a coarse powder.
5. Add the chili powder , salt and garlic to the powder and grind a bit. 
7. Store the Palli Podi in an airtight container.

Garnish:

Note: Add enough water while cooking, as the kadhi thickens upon cooling.

posts.fullCaption:
Perugu Vankaya (South Indian-style Dahi Baingan) A deliciously creamy, tangy brinjal (eggplant) curry with a South Indian twist — a perfect comfort dish to pair with hot rice or rotis!
Ingredients: Vegetables:
* Brinjal (eggplant) – 250 gms, sliced lengthwise
* Onion – 1, sliced lengthwise
For Marination:
* Thick yogurt – 1 small cup (100gms)
* Besan (gram flour) – 1 tablespoon
* Turmeric powder – ¼ tsp
* Ginger-garlic paste – 1 tablespoon
* Salt – ¼ tsp (or to taste)
* Coriander powder – 1 tbsp
* Cumin powder – ½ tbsp
* Jeerakharam (or red chili powder) – 1 tbsp
* A little oil for coating
Tempering:
* Mustard seeds – ½ tsp
* Cumin seeds – ½ tsp
* A pinch of hing (asafoetida)
* Curry leaves
Instructions:
1. In a bowl, whisk the yogurt with besan until smooth. Add ginger-garlic paste and all the dry spices. Mix well.
2. In another large bowl, toss the brinjal and onions with a little salt and oil. Add the yogurt-spice mixture and coat everything well.
3. Heat oil in a pan, add mustard seeds. Once they splutter, add cumin seeds, hing, and curry leaves.
4. Add the marinated brinjal-onion mix. Cover and cook on medium flame until the brinjal turns soft.
5. Remove the lid and cook uncovered till the oil separates and the gravy thickens. Garnish with fresh coriander leaves.Tips:
* If using a steel pan, stir frequently and cook on low-medium heat if using less oil.

posts.fullCaption:
Homemade Indian Yogurt (Curd/Dahi) Yogurt is an everyday essential in almost every South Indian meal! While it may seem simple to many Indians, this recipe is especially for my lovely Chinese friends who enjoy Indian yogurt and want to try making it at home.
Ingredients:
* 1 cup fresh milk (full cream or low fat)
* 1 tbsp fresh yogurt (as a starter culture)
Method:
1. Boil the milk thoroughly—this step is crucial whether you’re using fresh cow milk or pasteurized milk.
2. Allow the milk to cool until it’s warm (not hot). Optionally, strain the milk to remove the thick cream layer.
3. Add 1 tablespoon of fresh yogurt to the warm milk and stir gently.
4. Cover the bowl and keep it in a warm place for 5–6 hours or until the yogurt sets. (Setting time depends on your room temperature.)
5. For a quicker set, place a dry red chili on top—an age-old traditional tip!
Note: A good starter culture is key! The best results come from fresh, well-set yogurt. If you don’t have any, you can make a basic culture by adding a few drops of lemon juice or a slit green chili to warm milk. Let it sit in a warm spot for around 12 hours until it curdles. This can be used as a starter for your first batch—though it’s not suitable for eating on its own.
